correctness.rationale: The five-valued potential follows exactly from the two Laplacian eigenspace classes and solves the unit edge divergence at zero mean. Summation over all edge types yields F_N(a)+F_N(b), and the diagonal identity yields 1+H_N(a)+H_N(b) for the complement. A nonnegative product identity proves the top-two-parts rule for all r>=3, while the exact H_N ranking on K_{k,2,1} proves the strict reversed maximizing edge orbit and formulas for every k>=3. Direct exact rational Laplacian inversions reconstructed all 1572 columns of 86 graphs; 38 k cases were cross-checked. The universal conclusion relies on the analytical proof, not those finite experiments.

originality.rationale: The checked 2023 cycle-space paper computes invariant/minimal projections for graph products, especially tori and Hamming graphs, while the 2018 finite-metric-space paper treats quotient-space structure and recursively defined graph families. Neither inspected material supplies the additive edge-column norms for arbitrary complete multipartite graphs or the strict maximizing-edge reversal on K_{k,2,1}. An accessible published cactus-basis result computes suppression projections on transportation quotients, mathematically distinct from canonical orthogonal cut/cycle projections. Accessible earlier graph-projection findings involve bicliques, missing-edge or added-edge perturbations, or Cartesian graph products; their results do not entail the current all-multipartite closed formulas. Residual bibliographic risk persists.
residual_risks: A specialized or unindexed electrical-network source may have computed the same column norms under a transfer-current, Hodge, or sensitivity terminology.
Some published database records were accessible only as summaries; no whole-document noncoverage assertion is based on those snippets.
The result evaluates canonical orthogonal projections; a theorem about optimized arbitrary projections would require separate logical comparison and should not be conflated with it.

value.rationale: A natural operator-norm classification holds for every complete multipartite graph with at least three parts, and the two complementary endpoint norms use different part selection principles. The sharp and persistent K_{k,2,1} reversal plus equal positive exchange margins exposes a genuine structural boundary; these are neither isolated computations nor a restatement of the transfer-current pseudoinverse identity.
